metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Organ-function values or categories are optional; omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

provenance.note: 00586 specifies maximum 5–6 weekly cycles; confirm individual radiation course.

clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Use the most restrictive applicable component rule and confirm dose changes against the current official NCCP PDF.

treatment.schedule_summary: Concurrent radiotherapy and capecitabine Days 1–5 of each 7-day cycle, maximum 5–6 cycles. Radiation decisions require the radiation oncology plan.

diarrhoea_grade.label: Current diarrhoea grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: Usual bowel pattern.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: NCCP low-grade band: 2–3 extra stools/day; source nocturnal-stool wording overlaps grade 2.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: 4–6 extra stools/day or nocturnal stools (NCCP table 4).

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: 7–9 extra stools/day or incontinence (NCCP table 4).

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: 10 or more extra stools/day or grossly bloody diarrhoea; parenteral support may be needed (NCCP table 4).

diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: NCCP Table 4 uses legacy diarrhoea bands. Nocturnal stools appear in both low-grade and grade-2 rows: clarify the grade clinically. Assess hydration, stoma output, fever, pain and need for urgent care; do not grade by stool count alone.

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No oral mucositis.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Moderate pain or ulceration that does not interfere with oral intake; modified diet indicated.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Severe pain that interferes with oral intake.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

hand_foot_syndrome_grade.label: Palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia (hand-foot syndrome) grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No palmar–plantar erythrodysesthesia.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Minimal skin changes or dermatitis, such as erythema, oedema or hyperkeratosis, without pain.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Painful skin changes, including peeling, blisters, bleeding, fissures, oedema or hyperkeratosis; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Severe painful skin changes; limits self-care activities of daily living.

hand_foot_syndrome_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess skin changes, pain and impact on instrumental or self-care activities of daily living.

action.recommendation: Do not administer capecitabine in severe hepatic impairment: the supplementary capecitabine SmPC section 4.3 lists this as a contraindication. The NCCP table 2 statement about routine hepatic dose adjustment does not override that exclusion; resolve the plan with consultant/pharmacy.

rules.explanation: Do not administer capecitabine in severe hepatic impairment: the supplementary capecitabine SmPC section 4.3 lists this as a contraindication. The NCCP table 2 statement about routine hepatic dose adjustment does not override that exclusion; resolve the plan with consultant/pharmacy.

monitoring: FBC, renal and liver profile as specified by the current NCCP regimen
Treatment-specific toxicity monitoring before each administration/cycle

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Risk assigned from the most emetogenic active component and treatment phase.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
supportive_care.emetogenic_risk_note: Capecitabine: oral minimal-to-low risk. Radiotherapy-associated nausea depends on site and field and needs the radiation oncology plan. Follow local policy; provide rescue treatment and stop-and-call education.

administration.notes: With or within 30 minutes of food. Tablet strengths and final dose require pharmacy dose banding.

treatment_phases.notes: Concurrent radiotherapy and capecitabine Days 1–5 of each 7-day cycle, maximum 5–6 cycles. Radiation decisions require the radiation oncology plan.

capecitabine.-1: 75% of starting dose; final tablets pharmacy banded
capecitabine.-2: 50% of starting dose; final tablets pharmacy banded
